newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea wants N.Korean action after apology.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea wants N.Korean action after apology.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam, while welcoming a North Korean apology over a submarine incursion, urged Pyongyang on Tuesday to take specific steps to promote peace.
"It is action, rather than words, that counts," Kim told a New Year news conference.
He renewed a call for the communist North to join peace talks with South Korea, the United States and China, which he proposed last year jointly with U.S. president Bill Clinton.
North Korea has agreed to attend a preparatory briefing on the four-nation peace talks this month, he said. The briefing will be conducted by U.S. and South Korean officials.
"Within this month the three countries will meet for a briefing and we already have a promise from North Korea. But we don't know the time or the place yet," Kim said.
The session is designed to pave the way for talks aimed at securing a permanent peace arrangement on the Korean peninsula to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
But Kim cautioned against optimism for quick detente with North Korea and offered no new diplomatic initiatives in the New Year news conference, which he normally uses for unveiling major policies.
He said the submarine incursion into the South showed North Korea had not abandoned its dream of unifying Korea under communism.

The Shark-class submarine landed 26 armed agents on a Southern beach last September. North Korea apologised on December 29, and the following day South Korea returned the bodies of 24 of the infiltrators who were shot and killed during a massive manhunt.
One was captured alive and is in South Korean government custody, and the other is still at large.

Kim said famine-stricken North Korea faced many internal problems and it was not time to talk of an inter-Korean summit to discuss major steps for reunification of the peninsula, divided at the end of World War Two.
Kim stressed South Korea must build up its military strength to deter Northern aggression and encourage Pyongyang to seek accomodation with Seoul.
